open_obligations: Note that a martingale allows individual wrong-to-right cases, so any tension between the two is about averages.
Check that Du et al.'s agents satisfy condition (1).
Check whether Choi et al. report accuracy trajectories across debate rounds on tasks like Du et al.'s.

Note that Theorem 2 concerns modelled agents whose beliefs p_i,t follow the Bayesian update of Choi et al.'s DCM model, while Du et al.'s cases are debates between language models; check that Du et al.'s agents fit that model before comparing.
in.other_title: Multi-agent debate as a martingale: under condition (1), an agent's expected belief is unchanged
in.rationale: Du et al. conclude from qualitative cases where all agents start wrong but end right that debate does not only amplify an initially present correct answer. Choi, Zhu and Li prove that under their condition (1) an agent's belief sequence is a martingale: its expected belief at the next round equals its current belief; individual cases can still go wrong-to-right under a martingale.
in.scope: proposed SAME_QUESTION_DIFFERENT_SETTING: whether multi-agent debate does more than amplify initial answers, studied through expected beliefs under condition (1) by Choi, Zhu and Li and through qualitative debate examples by Du et al.
